findings.claim: All 48 practice questions are labelled '40 marks - Post-1914 Essay' but every mark scheme splits the 40 as AO1 (up to 20) + AO3 (up to 16) + AO4 (up to 4) and tops the ladder out at 'Top band (33-36)'.
findings.truth: The Edexcel post-1914 British play or novel question is 40 marks: AO1 16 + AO3 16 + AO4 8. A 20/16/4 split is an AQA-shaped guess, and the 36-mark ceiling miscalibrates every self-mark in the unit. Re-scaled to the house ladder across 40 (Top 33-40, Upper-mid 25-32, Mid 17-24, Lower-mid 9-16, Low 1-8) and the bottom band renamed from 'Lower band'. Lesson 1 question 1 also carried a 4-mark SPaG tail, re-scaled to 8.
findings.evidence: specs/edexcel/english-literature-1ET0.md raw-mark table (Component 1, questions 7 to 30: AO1 15/16, AO3 16, AO4 8, total 40) and the assessment summary ('Assessment Objectives covered are AO1, AO3 and AO4').

findings.claim: 'Component 1' (3 places), 'Section B' (11 places) and 'Level 5' (1 place) appear in lesson fields across lessons 1, 3, 7 and 8.
findings.truth: All three are on the house banned list and reject the whole unit at validation. Replaced with 'the Edexcel post-1914 novel essay' / 'this essay' and the house band wording 'top-band'.

findings.claim: 'The hens who protested against giving up their eggs confess to “having secreted six ears of corn” and are slaughtered on the spot', repeated as a flashcard ('What small crime do the hens confess to before being slaughtered?' - 'Secreting six ears of corn').
findings.truth: In chapter 7 the three hens confess that Snowball appeared to them in a dream and incited them to disobey Napoleon. The six ears of corn are a goose's confession. The flashcard marked the true answer against the wrong character.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg Australia ch. 7: 'The three hens ... stated that Snowball had appeared to them in a dream ... Then a goose came forward and confessed to having secreted six ears of corn during the last year's harvest'.

findings.claim: 'After Old Major dies, the animals - led by the pigs Napoleon and Snowball - drive Mr Jones from the farm.'
findings.truth: The Rebellion is spontaneous. Jones and his men fail to feed the animals, a cow breaks into the store-shed, and the animals turn on the men 'with one accord, though nothing of the kind had been planned beforehand'. The pigs take charge only afterwards - a point examiners reward.

findings.claim: 'Beasts of England' is replaced by 'a new song praising Napoleon himself' / 'a song praising Napoleon' - in lesson 4 prose, a lesson 4 knowledge-check stem, a lesson 2 mark scheme and lesson 7 prose.
findings.truth: Chapter 7: Minimus composes 'Animal Farm, Animal Farm, / Never through me shalt thou come to harm!' - it praises the farm, not the leader. The cult-of-personality piece is the separate chapter 8 poem 'Comrade Napoleon'.

findings.claim: The dogs 'wagging their tails at him in the same way as the other dogs had been used to do to Mr Jones', quoted in lessons 3 and 6; lesson 6 also places the line after the confessions scene.
findings.truth: Chapter 5 reads 'they wagged their tails to him in the same way as the other dogs had been used to do to Mr. Jones', and it comes immediately after Snowball is chased off, not after the chapter 7 executions.

findings.claim: Squealer's false statistics quoted as '“production has increased by 200 per cent”'.
findings.truth: The novella never uses that figure. Chapter 9: 'lists of figures proving that the production of every class of foodstuff had increased by two hundred per cent, three hundred per cent, or five hundred per cent'.

findings.claim: Exam stem: 'Snowball had been a brave fighter at the Battle of the Cowshed.'
findings.truth: Not in the novella. Boxer's chapter 7 line is 'Snowball fought bravely at the Battle of the Cowshed.' Edexcel stems are real quotations, so a fabricated stem teaches a wrong quotation for a closed-book exam.

findings.claim: Exam stem 'Suddenly, at a signal from Napoleon, all the dogs bounded forward...', with the mark scheme naming "the detail 'at a signal from Napoleon'".
findings.truth: Chapter 7 reads 'he uttered a high-pitched whimper. Immediately the dogs bounded forward, seized four of the pigs by the ear...'. The opening clause is invented, and the mark scheme then asks students to analyse it.

findings.claim: Exam stem 'Frederick and his men had already retreated... The animals had won, but they were weary and bleeding.'
findings.truth: Chapter 8 reads 'They had won, but they were weary and bleeding.' There is no 'Frederick and his men had already retreated' sentence - Frederick shouts to his men to get out and they run.

findings.claim: 'The pigs initially chase Moses away because he does no work and spreads distracting stories', repeated in a lesson 6 mark scheme.
findings.truth: Moses is never chased off. He 'sprang off his perch and flapped after her' when Mrs Jones fled at the Rebellion, and 'suddenly reappeared on the farm, after an absence of several years'. The pigs call his stories lies but let him stay on 'a gill of beer a day'.

findings.claim: Two exam stems put narrative framing inside the quotation marks: 'Napoleon announced that the name Animal Farm had been abolished...' (lesson 5) and 'Mr Pilkington had referred throughout to "Animal Farm." Napoleon... had referred to it as "The Manor Farm".' (lesson 7).
findings.truth: Chapter 10 reads 'the name "Animal Farm" had been abolished. Henceforward the farm was to be known as "The Manor Farm"', and Napoleon's actual sentence is 'He could not of course know ... that the name "Animal Farm" had been abolished.' Both stems trimmed to verbatim wording.

findings.claim: 'This kind of analysis scores highly on both AO1 and AO3.'
findings.truth: An AO code immediately followed by a full stop is rejected by the house validator as a spec-code pattern. Rewritten as '...AO1 and AO3 (context).'

findings.claim: 'For a modern-text essay, you will usually respond to a prompt ... Check your exam board's specimen paper for the exact format, timing, and mark allocation.'
findings.truth: Board-agnostic placeholder on a board-specific unit. The format is fixed and known: ONE essay from a choice of two, each preceded by a short quotation, 40 marks, closed book, about 50 minutes.
findings.evidence: specs/edexcel/english-literature-1ET0.md, Component 1 overview and assessment summary.

findings.claim: 'Which AO1/AO3/AO4 Assessment Objective is NOT tested in Edexcel Section B?' - answer 'AO2'.
findings.truth: The stem lists only the three objectives that ARE tested, so the keyed answer is not among the options offered by the question. Reworded to ask which objective is not tested; the answer is unchanged.
findings.evidence: specs/edexcel/english-literature-1ET0.md: 'Assessment Objectives covered are AO1, AO3 and AO4.'

findings.claim: 'What Russian name did Stalin give the state newspaper that means "truth"?'
findings.truth: Pravda was founded in 1912 and Stalin did not name it; he was one of its early editors. The prose in the same lesson is correct, so only the flashcard stem needed rewording.
findings.evidence: Lesson 1 prose already says only that Stalin's regime used Pravda for propaganda.

findings.claim: 'He has food tasters and surrounds himself with dogs at all times.'
findings.truth: One young pig, Pinkeye, is 'given the task of tasting all his food before he ate it, lest it should be poisoned' (ch. 8). The plural overstates it, but 'food tasters' is the <dfn> term keyed to the glossary entry, so an edit would break the glossary link for a point that costs no marks.

findings.claim: T.S. Eliot 'rejected it on the grounds that it was “not the right point of view from which to criticise the political situation.”'
findings.truth: Eliot's 1944 letter reads 'we have no conviction ... that this is the right point of view from which to criticise the political situation at the present time.' The lesson inverts it into a direct quotation. The sense is preserved and no mark depends on the exact wording, so it is recorded rather than edited.

findings.claim: 'Napoleon declares it a “great victory,” which Squealer supports with propaganda.'
findings.truth: In chapter 8 it is Squealer who insists on the victory against Boxer's doubts, and the narrator says that after Napoleon's speech 'it did seem to them after all that they had won a great victory'. The roles are mildly reversed, but the analytical point stands.

findings.claim: 'Throughout these chapters, the Seven Commandments are quietly altered', then lists 'No animal shall sleep in a bed with sheets'.
findings.truth: The bed commandment is altered in chapter 6, outside this lesson's chapters 7-8. The alcohol and killing clauses are chapter 8. Too small to be worth disturbing a narration block.

findings.claim: Six of the eight lesson descriptions are 100 characters or longer (lesson 2 is 104, lesson 3 is 102, lesson 4 is 117, lesson 6 is 107, lesson 7 is 110, lesson 8 is 109).
findings.truth: Not a fact error, so nothing is edited, but the house validator caps a lesson description under 100 characters and only 7 of 59 descriptions in the sister Edexcel units breach it. Flagged in case the apply step validates untouched fields.
findings.evidence: Character counts taken from the unit's own _raw.json.

summary: Every one of the 48 practice questions carries an AQA-shaped AO split (AO1 20 / AO3 16 / AO4 4) on a ladder that stops at 36, when the Edexcel post-1914 essay is 40 marks split AO1 16 / AO3 16 / AO4 8 - that is the largest finding, and 14 banned spec codes ('Component 1', 'Section B', 'Level 5') would reject the unit at validation. The exam prose is otherwise sound: the unit already teaches one essay from a choice of two, a quotation stimulus, closed book and no AO2. The text errors are five fabricated or reshaped exam-stem quotations, the six ears of corn given to the hens instead of the goose, the replacement anthem said to praise Napoleon when it praises the farm, and Moses said to be chased off the farm.
